traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Didiereaceae: leaves alternate; leaves simple; stipules absent; plants dioecious or polygamous; ovary superior; stems woody; flowers in cymes; perianth sepals and petals; stamens 8 (-10); carpels (2-) 3 (-4). Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.woodiness.note: German Wikipedia, 'Didiereaceae' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): succulent, thick-stemmed shrubs or trees, often cactus-like in build.

traits.life_span.note: German Wikipedia, 'Didiereaceae' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): shrubs and trees, so perennial; English Wikipedia: Didiereoideae shrubs and trees 2-20 m.

traits.leaf_division.note: Kept from the library family file (Watson and Dallwitz DELTA data): leaves simple; nothing read contradicts it.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: German Wikipedia, 'Didiereaceae' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): long-shoot leaves small and soon falling; the short-shoot leaves stand in decussate (opposite) pairs and last one growing season. English Wikipedia 'Didiereaceae': in Didiereoideae the short-shoot leaves come singly or in pairs. So both, not alternate alone.

traits.short_shoots.note: German Wikipedia, 'Didiereaceae' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): branches start as long shoots, and short shoots develop in their leaf axils; leaves and spines come from these areole-like short shoots.

traits.stipules.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): German Wikipedia 'Portulacaria afra' says stipules absent; the family file's DELTA 'stipules absent' is kept.

traits.sexual_system.note: German Wikipedia, 'Didiereaceae' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): Calyptrotheca and Portulacaria have only bisexual flowers; Decarya female and bisexual; all other genera (Didiereoideae) unisexual and dioecious. By species roughly 11 dioecious to 9 bisexual, so both 'often'.

traits.ovary_position.note: German Wikipedia, 'Didiereaceae' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): carpels united into a superior, one-chambered ovary.

traits.inflorescence.note: German Wikipedia, 'Didiereaceae' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): inflorescences from the areoles, branching forked or umbel-like (cymose); the file's 'cyme' kept.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: English Wikipedia, 'Didiereaceae' (read 2026-10-19, lower trust): Didiereoideae flowers radially symmetric; German Wikipedia: Portulacaria flowers small and regular.

traits.perianth.note: German Wikipedia, 'Didiereaceae' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): flowers with a double perianth: only two sepals, free and often unequal; petals four (Didiereoideae) or five, free or (Portulacaria) united. English Wikipedia instead calls them four tepals with two basal bracts in Didiereoideae.

traits.stamens.note: German Wikipedia, 'Didiereaceae' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): Didiereoideae two whorls of four or five stamens; Ceraria one whorl of five; Portulacaria mostly four to seven, rarely to ten; Calyptrotheca many (uncounted).

traits.carpels.note: German Wikipedia, 'Didiereaceae' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): usually three, rarely two or four carpels, a long style with a usually three-lobed stigma; matches the file's (2-)3(-4).

traits.fruit_type.note: German Wikipedia, 'Didiereaceae' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): a dry, more or less three-angled capsule with one seed, wrapped in the persistent pair of sepals; in Portulacaria (German Wikipedia 'Portulacaria') the fruit is a dry three-winged fruit that does not open, read here as a samara.

traits.calyx_in_fruit.note: German Wikipedia, 'Didiereaceae' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): the fruit is enclosed by the persistent pair of sepals.
